B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024 1 Crl.A.No.1303/2024 KABC010203202024 IN THE COURT OF THE LX ADDITIONAL CITY CIVIL & SESSIONS JUDGE, BENGALURU (CCH-61) DATED THIS THE 7th DAY OF DECEMBER 2024 :PRESENT: Sri Prakash S.Helavar, B.Com., LL.M., LX Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru. CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 1303/2024 APPELLANT :- Mrs.B.M.Rohini W/o Sri.B.S.Mukund Aged about 40 years, R/at No.4162 Tower 4, Phoenix One Bangalore West Apartments Dr.Rajkumar Road, Bengaluru 560 010. (Rep by Sri.S.S, - Advocate) V/s RESPONDENT :- Sri.B.S.Mukund S/o B.S.Srinivas Aged about 42 years R/at No.53, 16th Cross, 10th Main, Near MES College, Malleswaram, Bengaluru 560 055. (Rep by Sri MBGG- Advocate) 2 Crl.A.No.1303/2024 JUDGMENT Rohini. B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51896706/ 1 The present appeal is filed by the appellant- petitioner under Section 29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 requesting to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order dated 06.05.2024 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court -III, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc No.178/2023 and consequently allow the interim applications No.1 to 4 filed by the appellant i.e., IA No.1 under Section 23 r/w 19(1)(A) and (D), I.A. No.2 under Section 23 R/w 19(1)(a) and 2, IA No.4 under Section 19(1) (f) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 on the following: GROUNDS (a) That the impugned order is wholly illegal and unjust subjecting the Appellant to manifest injustice. (b) The Hon'ble Trial court has not appreciated the materials available on record properly and correctly and has therefore exercised jurisdiction with material irregularity. The impugned order passed by the Hon'ble Trial Court is arbitrary, illegal and grossly Crl.A.No.1303/2024 unjust. The impugned order is bereft of any valid and cogent reasoning. The same is therefore liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. (c) The Hon'ble Trial Court below has gravely erred by not considering the assets and liabilities along with the documents produced by the Appellant. The Hon'ble Trial Court also perfunctorily rejected the Interim applications No 1 to 4 filed by the Appellant i.e I.A.No.1- Application U/s 23 R/w 19 (1)(A) and (D), I.A.No.2 U/s 23 R/w 20 (1)(B) and (D), I.A.No.3- U/s 23 R/w 19 (1)(a) and (2), I.A.No.4- U/s 19(1) (f) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which reads as follows: "The IA Nos. I to IV filed by the Appellant u/s 23 r/w sec 19(1)(a) & (d), sec 23 r/w sec 20(1) (b) (d), sec 23 r/w 19(1) (a) & (2) and sec 19 (1) (f) of PWDV Act is hereby rejected. Further, the respondent no 1 is hereby directed to pay the school expenses of children if Appellant furnished necessary documents regarding school expenses". (d) The Hon'ble Trial Court has strangely observed in its order dated 06.05.2024 that "On perusal of the affidavit of assets and liabilities Crl.A.No.1303/2024 furnished by the Appellant, it appears that the Appellant is not having any source of income". Subsequently, the Hon'ble Trial Court has further observed that "On perusal of the affidavit of assets and liabilities of both the parties it appears that both the parties have suppressed their income as well as their expenditure". (e) It is contended that at one hand the Hon'ble Trail Court has recorded that the Appellant has no source of income and that the Respondent is earning a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- per month, while on the other hand goes on to state that the parties have suppressed their incomes, the Hon'ble Trial Court has made contradictory statements in the order and failed to appreciate the fact that when the Rohini. B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51896706/ 2 Appellant has no source of income the question of suppressing the income does not arise. Thus the view taken by the Hon'ble Trial Court is grossly incorrect and quite contradictory to its own findings and liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Furthermore, the Respondent had come on record and filed his objections to the Interim applications No 1 to 4 filed by the Appellant i.e I.A.No. 1- Application U/s 23 R/w 19 (1)(A) and (D), I.A.No.2 - U/s 23 R/w 20 (1)(B) and (D), I.A.No.3- U/s 23 R/w 19 (1)(a) and (2), I.A.No.4- U/s 19(1) (f) of the Protection of Crl.A.No.1303/2024 Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 wherein the Respondent himself has agreed to take care of the children's expenses and that he is currently paying a sum of Rs. 60,000/- per month towards the children's expenses. The same has been recorded by the Hon'ble Trial court in its impugned order. The Hon'ble Trial court has further made findings to the effect that "the Respondent No. 1 being the father of the children, he is having bounden duty to take care the welfare of his children if the Respondent no.1 is directed to look over the educational expenses of his children, no hardships would be caused to him." However the Trial court in the final order has rejected all the applications leaving a wide scope of ambiguity in the impugned order, as at one stretch the Trial Court has rejected the applications and at the next very point orders that "the Respondent No.1 is directed to pay the school expenses of children if Appellant furnished necessary documents regarding school expenses". The impugned order is capricious, pervaded with ambiguity and uncertainty and liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. (f) It is contended that the Appellant and the children reached out to Respondent No.1 vide Whatsapp asking him to pay for the expenses and also sent him the necessary documents and receipts for the Crl.A.No.1303/2024 expenses incurred regarding the school and other co- curricular activities in terms of the aforementioned order, however the Respondent No.1 has neither bothered to pay for the children's expenses nor replied to the messages sent to him even after he has viewed the messages. This clearly indicates the intentions of the Respondent No.1 and how he has been shying away from taking responsibility of his own children and the ambiguity in the impugned order only encourages the Respondent to harass the Appellant and the children even further. (g) It is further contended that while the Respondent has commenced paying for some of the children's educational expenses, it is pertinent to note that the Respondent, who has declared before the Hon'ble Trial Court that his monthly income is approximately Rs.80,000/- has ironically been able to cover expenses cumulatively exceeding Rs.3,00,000/- in a single month for the children's needs. Despite this, the Respondent is refusing to pay the children's tuition fees, contending that it does not fall under the children's educational expenses. This refusal is particularly concerning, as tuition fees are an integral part of educational expenses, and the Respondent's refusal to pay undermines the children's right to Crl.A.No.1303/2024 proper education. It is pertinent to note that the interim reliefs which were sought by the Appellant are very crucial and vital as the Appellant alone is unable to bear the educational expenses of both the children and also is in no position to pay the monthly rentals of the present rented house. The Appellant was forced to take the present place of residence on rent as she had no other place to move to on such short notice and considered the welfare of the children in terms of their extracurricular activities and tuition as a paramount condition so that their day to day lifestyle and education is not affected in any manner. The Trial Court had observed that "at this juncture, the reliefs sought by the Appellant has to be considered after a full fledge trial by both the sides along with the main petition"; it is relevant to mention that the Appellant has filed an application for an interim maintenance as she is unable to bear the Rohini. B M vs B S Mukund on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51896706/ 3 expenditure, such being the case the Trial Court observing that 'the reliefs sought by the Appellant has to be considered after a full fledge trial' is unjust as it defeats the purpose of filing such application. As such the Trial Court dismissing the applications filed by the Appellant without proper considering the subject matter is harsh, unjust and arbitrary. Hence, the order dated 06.05.2024 is liable to be set-side on this score by itself. Crl.A.No.1303/2024 (h) The Appellant had relied on the certain judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka i.e., Shivakumar Vs Parvathi- Crl.R.P. No.2000004/15. Deepali lengede Vs Sandeep Lengade- WP.2688/23.
texts.facts: ( j ) The Trial Court committed grave error of law in overlooking the gravity of the situation and not appreciated that the object of filing of interim applications and seeking interim reliefs would be Crl.A.No.1303/2024 defeated by dismissing the said application and the Appellant is unable to be able to sustain the expenses of the children or herself and the Respondent has completely abandoned the Appellant and the children and has taken no responsibility in maintaining them or helping them to live their lives peacefully. (k) Cumulatively, the impugned order dated 06.05.2024 passed by the Trial Court is illegal, unjust and technically unsound and the same is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the Criminal Petition filed by the Appellant requires to be allowed by this Court as prayed for. However, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka vide order dated 24.07.2024 disposed off the Crl.P 5527/2024 by granting liberty to challenge the impugned order before this Court. So, the notice was issued to the respondent. The Appellant and Respondent have been married since 18.08.2006. The marriage is also registered under the Hindu Marriage Act. Almost immediately after moving into the matrimonial house, the Respondent who was ably influenced by his parents created a very hostile environment at the matrimonial home and tortured the Appellant by using profane and vulgar language.
texts.arguments: When the Appellant requested him to buy her a car to drop and pick up their children from school, the Respondent refused to buy her a car stating that the Respondent cannot afford it even though the Respondent was more than capable of affording the same. It is contended that since the Appellant is a housewife and she has no source of income to Crl.A.No.1303/2024 maintain herself and her children, the Appellant is dependent on her brother and her parents who are senior citizens for the Appellants day to day expenses.
